newsitem.title: USA: EU, US studying new proposals to settle meat row.
newsitem.headline: EU, US studying new proposals to settle meat row.

text.p: The United States and European Union will not resume talks to resolve a bitter dispute over meat imports until next Wednesday, the senior U.S. negotiator at the talks told Reuters Wednesday.

EU negotiators had been expected to return to Washington today to resume discussions, but Drazek said the decision was made last night that both sides needed more time to study proposals that were offered this past weekend.
"We decided last night that it would serve our purposes better if we had more time to prepare on both sides for the next series of discussions," Drazek said in a short interview.
Drazek said the two sides will continue to communicate via the telephone and faxes in the interum.
So far, meetings have been scheduled for next Wednesday and Thursday, Drazek said. He indicated that the talks could go longer if progress is being made.
Drazek would not not comment on any of the proposals that have been discussed since the negotiators last sat down together last week.
"I think it would be better if we had a chance to talk to them...I don't want to complicate our negotiations next week," Drazek said.
Drazek said the biggest problems in the veterinary equivalency talks remain with poultry issues, but also noted that "there are issues still outstanding in red meat as well."
USDA officials are continuing to stay in close touch with the U.S. poultry and red meat industries to get their views, Drazek said.
The U.S. and EU have been trying to settle a years-old dispute over meat import inspection regulation.
The dispute has already disrupted U.S. poultry shipments to Europe, and could halt some $300 million worth of European meat products to the U.S. if a settlement is not reached.

Washington had threatened to remove more than 100 European meat and poultry packing plants from its list of approved exporters by April 15, but on Tuesday extended that deadline to April 30 in hopes an agreement would be reached by then.
Drazek would not comment on any options being considered right now.
